oracletemplate.arrowhurwicz.arrowhurwiczuniformrate.result related arrow–hurwicz for bounded composite saddles we consider the saddle objective \(\phi(x,y)=g(x)+\langle y,kx\rangle-h(y)\) on convex sets \(x\subset e\) and \(y\subset f\) , where \(e,f\) are real inner product spaces. both sets lie in balls of radius \(r>0\) about zero; \(g:e\to\mathbb{r}\) and \(h:f\to\mathbb{r}\) are convex and \(m\) -lipschitz on their respective sets, with \(m\geq0\) , and \(k:e\to f\) is bounded linear with operator norm at most \(l>0\) . the oracle returns exact linear-map, adjoint, and constrained proximal evaluations. from given feasible points, arrow–hurwicz must return a feasible pair \((\bar{x},\bar{y})\) satisfying \(\phi(\bar{x},y)-\phi(x,\bar{y})\leq\varepsilon\) for every \((x,y)\in x\times y\) , almost surely, where \(\varepsilon>0\) is the tolerance. the optimization problem is \[\inf {x\in x}\sup {y\in y}\phi(x,y).\] the norms on \(e\) and \(f\) are induced by their inner products, and we use the product norm \(\|(x,y)\|=\max\{\|x\|,\|y\|\}\) . operator norms are the induced operator norms. the algorithm receives \(e,f,x,y,r,l,m,\varepsilon\) and the starting points \(x^0,y^0\) ; access to \(k,g,h\) is through the oracle. our assumptions: assumption 1 (bounded feasible sets). the sets \(x\) and \(y\) are convex, \(x^0\in x\) , \(y^0\in y\) , and \[\begin{aligned} \|x\|&\leq r &&\text{for every }x\in x,\\ \|y\|&\leq r &&\text{for every }y\in y. \end{aligned}\] assumption 2 (convex composite objective). the functions \(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(x\) and \(y\) , respectively, and satisfy \[\begin{aligned} |g(a)-g(b)|&\leq m\|a-b\| &&(a,b\in x),\\ |h(a)-h(b)|&\leq m\|a-b\| &&(a,b\in y). \end{aligned}\] the map \(k:e\to f\) is bounded linear with \(\|k\| {\mathrm{op}}\leq l\) . there exists a map \(k^*:f\to e\) satisfying \[\langle k^*y,z\rangle=\langle y,kz\rangle, \qquad y\in f,\ z\in e.\] assumption 3 (exact proximal access). for every \(u\in e\) , \(v\in f\) , and \(t>0\) , the oracle provides points \[\begin{aligned} p x(u,t)&\in\operatorname*{arg\,min} {x\in x} \left\{t g(x)+\tfrac12\|x-u\|^2\right\},\\ p y(v,t)&\in\operatorname*{arg\,min} {y\in y} \left\{t h(y)+\tfrac12\|y-v\|^2\right\}. \end{aligned}\] the oracle also returns \(kx\) for any \(x\in e\) and \(k^*y\) for any \(y\in f\) . each linear-map, adjoint, or proximal evaluation counts as one call to the same oracle. proximal queries accept arbitrary real \(t\) , with the stated minimization requirement applying when \(t>0\) . our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze arrow–hurwicz with a constant step size \(\eta>0\) chosen from the available inputs. starting from the given pair \((x^0,y^0)\) , the updates are \[\begin{aligned} x^{k+1}&=p x\bigl(x^k-\eta k^*y^k,\eta\bigr),\\ y^{k+1}&=p y\bigl(y^k+\eta kx^{k+1},\eta\bigr), \qquad k\geq0. \end{aligned}\] each iteration makes four calls, in the order \(k^*y^k\) , the primal proximal evaluation, \(kx^{k+1}\) , and the dual proximal evaluation. after \(n\geq1\) complete iterations, the output is \[\bar{x}=\frac1n\sum {k=1}^{n}x^k, \qquad \bar{y}=\frac1n\sum {k=1}^{n}y^k.\] if the call budget ends during a subsequent iteration, that incomplete iteration is excluded from the averages. if no iteration has been completed, the output is the current pair: \((x^0,y^0)\) after zero or one call, and \((x^1,y^0)\) after two or three calls. the required accuracy is feasibility together with a uniform primal–dual gap bound: \[\begin{gathered} (\bar{x},\bar{y})\in x\times y,\\ \phi(\bar{x},y)-\phi(x,\bar{y})\leq\varepsilon \quad\text{for every }x\in x,\ y\in y, \qquad p\text{-a.s.}, \end{gathered}\] where \(p\) is the law of the algorithm’s randomness; the specified arrow–hurwicz method and its oracle replies are deterministic. 4 \cdot \left\lceil \left(\frac{11 \cdot r \cdot \left(l \cdot r + m\right)}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{4}{3}} \right\rceil {+} 0 space \(e\) . the map is \(\rho\) -cohypomonotone, where \(\rho\geq 0\) , and its derivative \(j(x)=df(x)\) is \(h\) -lipschitz in operator norm, where \(h>0\) . a given starting point \(x^0\in e\) lies within distance \(r>0\) of a zero \(x^\star\) of \(f\) . the oracle returns \((f(x),j(x))\) at \(x\) . for a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) , the goal is an output \(\bar{x}\in e\) satisfying \(\|f(\bar{x})\|\leq\varepsilon\) almost surely under \(p\) , the law of the algorithm’s randomness. the root-finding problem is to find \(x\in e\) such that \[f(x)=0.\] write \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\) for the inner product and \(\|\cdot\|\) for its induced norm; \(\|\cdot\| {\mathrm{op}}\) denotes the induced operator norm for linear maps from \(e\) to \(e\) . the algorithm receives \(e\) , \(h\) , \(\rho\) , \(r\) , \(\varepsilon\) , and \(x^0\) . our assumptions: assumption 1 (lipschitz derivative). the map \(f\) is fréchet differentiable everywhere on \(e\) , with derivative \(j(x):e\to e\) , and \[\|j(x)-j(y)\| {\mathrm{op}}\leq h\|x-y\|, \qquad x,y\in e.\] assumption 2 (cohypomonotonicity). for every \(x,y\in e\) , \[\langle f(x)-f(y),x-y\rangle \geq -\rho\|f(x)-f(y)\|^2.\] assumption 3 (initial distance to a zero). there exists \(x^\star\in e\) such that \[\begin{aligned} f(x^\star)&=0,\\ \|x^0-x^\star\|&\leq r. \end{aligned}\] queries may be made at any point of \(e\) , and both components of the oracle reply are exact. after the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy the residual criterion \[\|f(\bar{x})\|\leq\varepsilon \quad by catalog unresolved comparison longtails.theorems.comparisonorthconvex oracletemplate.comparisonorth.result none comparison-based smooth convex minimization we consider minimizing a differentiable convex function \(f:\mathbb{r}^n\to\mathbb{r}\) , where \(n\geq 1\) is an integer. its gradient is \(l\) -lipschitz in the euclidean norm, with \(l>0\) , and a given starting point \(x^0\in\mathbb{r}^n\) lies within distance \(r>0\) of a global minimizer \(x^\star\) . at a queried pair \((x,y)\) , the oracle returns the boolean value of \(f(x)\leq f(y)\) . for a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) , the goal is an output \(\bar{x}\in\mathbb{r}^n\) satisfying \(f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)\leq\varepsilon\) almost surely under \(p\) , the law of the algorithm’s randomness. the optimization problem is \[\min {x\in\mathbb{r}^n} f(x).\] throughout, \(\|\cdot\|\) denotes the euclidean norm. the algorithm receives \(n\) , \(l\) , \(r\) , \(\varepsilon\) , and \(x^0\) . our assumptions: assumption 1 (convexity). for every \(x,y\in\mathbb{r}^n\) and \(t\in[0,1]\) , \[f((1-t)x+ty)\leq (1-t)f(x)+t f(y).\] assumption 2 (smoothness). the function \(f\) is differentiable everywhere on \(\mathbb{r}^n\) , and its gradient satisfies \[\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|\leq l\|x-y\|, \qquad x,y\in\mathbb{r}^n.\] assumption 3 (initial distance). there exists match convex ball proximal minimization we minimize a convex function \(f:e\to\mathbb{r}\) over a convex set \(c\) in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space \(e\) , with closed constrained epigraph. a given \(x^0\in c\) satisfies \(\|x^0-x^\star\|\leq r\) and \(f(x^0)-f(x^\star)\leq\delta\) for a minimizer \(x^\star\in c\) , where \(r\geq0\) and \(\delta>0\) . at \(x\in c\) , the oracle returns an exact minimizer over \(\{z\in c:\|z-x\|\leq t\}\) , where \(t>0\) . ball proximal iteration must return \(\bar{x}\in c\) with \(f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)\leq\varepsilon\) almost surely under \(p\) , the law of oracle randomness, for \(\varepsilon>0\) . the optimization problem is \[\min {x\in c} f(x).\] the norm \(\|\cdot\|\) is induced by the inner product on \(e\) . the algorithm receives \(e\) , \(t\) , \(r\) , \(\delta\) , \(\varepsilon\) , and \(x^0\) ; the set \(c\) and function \(f\) are accessed through the oracle. our assumptions: assumption 1 (convexity and closed epigraph). the set \(c\subseteq e\) is convex, and for all \(x,y\in c\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\) , \[f((1-\lambda)x+\lambda y) \leq (1-\lambda)f(x)+\lambda f(y).\] the constrained epigraph \[\{(x,a)\in e\times\mathbb{r}:x\in c,\ f(x)\leq a\}\] is closed in \(e\times\mathbb{r}\) . assumption 2 (initialization and minimizer). the given starting point satisfies \(x^0\in c\) . there exists \(x^\star\in c\) such that \[\begin{aligned} f(x^\star)&\leq f(x) &&\text{for every }x\in c,\\ \|x^0-x^\star\|&\leq r,\\ f(x^0)-f(x^\star)&\leq\delta. \end{aligned}\] assumption 3 (exact ball proximal oracle). for every query \(x\in c\) , every oracle reply \(y\) satisfies \[\begin{aligned} y&\in c, & \|y-x\|&\leq t,\\ f(y)&\leq f(z) &&\text{for all }z\in c\text{ with }\|z-x\|\leq t. \end{aligned}\] these conditions hold for every query history and every realization of the oracle randomness. the oracle may select among multiple minimizers using that history and randomness. our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze ball proximal iteration with fixed radius \(t\) . starting at the given \(x^0\) , each step queries the oracle at the current iterate and replaces it by the returned point: \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min} {\substack{z\in c\\\|z-x^k\|\leq t}} f(z), \qquad k=0,\ldots,k-1.\] here \(k\geq0\) is the integer oracle-call budget, each step uses one call, and the output is the last iterate \(\bar{x}=x^k\) . all queries therefore lie in \(c\) . the required accuracy is \[\bar{x}\in c, \qquad f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)\leq\varepsilon \quad p\text{-a.s.}\] the minimizer \(x^\star\) is fixed independently of the oracle randomness. \left\lceil \min\left\{ \left(\frac{r}{t}\right)^{2}, \frac{r}{t} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{\max\left\{ 0, \(f:\mathbb{r}^d\to\mathbb{r}\) , where \(d\geq1\) and \(l>0\) . a global minimizer \(x^\star\) satisfies \(\|x^\star\|\leq r\) , where \(r>0\) and \(\|\cdot\|\) is the euclidean norm. the oracle returns an unbiased stochastic subgradient using independent, identically distributed samples, with noise variance at most \(\sigma^2/d\) in every unit direction, where \(\sigma\geq0\) . for \(\varepsilon>0\) , the goal is a measurable output \(\bar{x}\) satisfying \(f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)\leq\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(2/3\) under \(p\) , the joint law of the oracle samples and independent algorithm randomness. the optimization problem is \[\min {x\in\mathbb{r}^d} f(x).\] write \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\) for the euclidean inner product. the algorithm receives \(d\in\mathbb{n} {\geq1}\) , \(l>0\) , \(r>0\) , \(\sigma\geq0\) , \(\varepsilon>0\) , and the measurable sample space \(\omega\) . our assumptions: assumption 1 (convexity and lipschitz continuity). for every \(x,y\in\mathbb{r}^d\) and \(t\in[0,1]\) , \[\begin{aligned} f((1-t)x+ty)&\leq(1-t)f(x)+tf(y),\\ |f(x)-f(y)|&\leq l\|x-y\|. \end{aligned}\] assumption 2 (bounded minimizer). there exists \(x^\star\in\mathbb{r}^d\) such that \[\begin{aligned} f(x^\star)&\leq f(x) &&\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{r}^d,\\ \|x^\star\|&\leq r. \end{aligned}\] assumption 3 (stochastic subgradients and covariance). there exist a probability measure \(p\) on \(\omega\) , a map \(v:\mathbb{r}^d\to\mathbb{r}^d\) , and a jointly measurable map \(g:\mathbb{r}^d\times\omega\to\mathbb{r}^d\) . for every \(x\in\mathbb{r}^d\) , the map \(g(x,\cdot)\) is bochner integrable under \(p\) , and \(\|g(x,\cdot)-v(x)\|^2\) is integrable under \(p\) . for all \(x,y,u\in\mathbb{r}^d\) , \[\begin{aligned} \mathbb{e} {\xi\sim p}[g(x,\xi)]&=v(x),\\ \langle v(x),y-x\rangle&\leq f(y)-f(x),\\ \mathbb{e} {\xi\sim p}\big[\langle g(x,\xi)-v(x),u\rangle^2\big] &\leq \frac{\sigma^2}{d}\|u\|^2. \end{aligned}\] at call \(k\geq0\) , a query \(x\in\mathbb{r}^d\) receives \(g(x,\xi k)\) . the sample variables \((\xi k) {k\geq0}\) are measurable, mutually independent, and each has law \(p\) . the algorithm’s randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence. queries may be made at any point of \(\mathbb{r}^d\) . after the allotted oracle calls, the output \(\bar{x}\in\mathbb{r}^d\) must be measurable and satisfy \[p\bigl(f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)>\varepsilon\bigr)\leq\frac13.\] \left\lceil 2^{32} \cdot \left(d + \frac{\sigma^{2} \cdot r^{2}}{\varepsilon^{2}}\right) \cdot \left(1 + longtails.theorems.noneuclideanweakmintyextragradient.result none non-euclidean weak minty problems we seek a zero of an operator \(f:e\to e^*\) on a finite-dimensional real normed space \(e\) , where \(e^*\) is its continuous dual with induced operator norm \(\|\cdot\| {\mathrm{op}}\) . the operator is \(l\) -lipschitz, with \(l>0\) , and satisfies a weak minty condition with parameter \(0\leq\rho\leq 1/(20l)\) at a zero \(x^\star\) . a differentiable, \(\mu\) -strongly convex function \(h:e\to\mathbb{r}\) , with \(\mu>0\) , bounds the bregman distance from a given \(x^0\in e\) to \(x^\star\) by \(d\geq0\) . the oracle returns \(f(x)\) at \(x\) . for \(\varepsilon>0\) , the goal is an output \(\bar{x}\in e\) satisfying \(\|f(\bar{x})\| {\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon\) almost surely under \(p\) , the law of the algorithm’s randomness. the problem is to find \(x\in e\) such that \[f(x)=0.\] write \(\langle v,u\rangle=v(u)\) for \(v\in e^*\) and \(u\in e\) . the norm on \(e\) is denoted by \(\|\cdot\|\) , and define the bregman divergence by \[b h(u,x)=h(u)-h(x)-\langle h'(x),u-x\rangle,\] where \(h'(x)\in e^*\) is the fréchet derivative. the algorithm receives \(e\) , \(l\) , \(\rho\) , \(\mu\) , \(h\) , and \(x^0\) ; the bound \(d\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\) may enter only the oracle-call budget. our assumptions: assumption 1 (bregman geometry). the function \(h\) is fréchet differentiable everywhere on \(e\) , and \[b h(u,x)\geq\frac{\mu}{2}\|u-x\|^2, \qquad x,u\in e.\] assumption 2 (lipschitz continuity). the operator satisfies \[\|f(x)-f(y)\| {\mathrm{op}}\leq l\|x-y\|, \qquad x,y\in e.\] assumption 3 (weak minty condition and initial bound). there exists \(x^\star\in e\) such that \[\begin{aligned} f(x^\star)&=0,\\ b h(x^\star,x^0)&\leq d,\\ \langle f(x),x-x^\star\rangle &\geq-\rho\|f(x)\| {\mathrm{op}}^2, \qquad x\in e. \end{aligned}\] queries may be made at any point of \(e\) . after the allotted oracle calls, the output must satisfy the residual criterion \[\|f(\bar{x})\| {\mathrm{op}}\leq\varepsilon \quad p\text{-a.s.}\] 2 + 2 \cdot \left\lceil \frac{400 \cdot l^{2} \cdot d}{\mu \cdot \varepsilon^{2}} \right\rceil {+} 0 \(\varepsilon\) through any unilateral pure-action deviation. write \[\delta d=\left\{z\in\mathbb{r}^d:z i\geq 0\text{ for all }i,\ \sum {i=1}^d z i=1\right\}.\] the players maximize the respective payoffs \(x^\top ay\) and \(x^\top cy\) over \(x\in\delta m\) and \(y\in\delta n\) . the algorithm receives only \(m\) , \(n\) , and \(\varepsilon\) ; the bound \(b\) may enter the oracle-call budget but is not an algorithm input. our assumptions: assumption 1 (bounded exact potential). there exists a matrix \(h\in\mathbb{r}^{m\times n}\) such that, for all \(i,i'\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(j,j'\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) , \[\begin{aligned} 0\leq h {ij}&\leq b,\\ a {ij}-a {i'j}&=h {ij}-h {i'j},\\ c {ij}-c {ij'}&=h {ij}-h {ij'}. \end{aligned}\] queries may be made at any &&j=1,\ldots,n. \end{aligned}\] the setup is algorithm-specific: we analyze regret matching+ with simultaneous updates and retention of the most recent pair passing the deviation test. for \(d\geq 1\) and \(q\in\mathbb{r}^d\) , define \[s d(q) i= \begin{cases} q i\big/\sum {\ell=1}^d q \ell,&\displaystyle\sum {\ell=1}^d q \ell>0,\\ 1/d,&\displaystyle\sum {\ell=1}^d q \ell\leq 0. \end{cases}\] initialize the two regret vectors as \(q^0=0\in\mathbb{r}^m\) and \(r^0=0\in\mathbb{r}^n\) , and initialize the retained pair as \[z^0=(s m(0),s n(0)).\] at iteration \(t\geq 0\) , query \[\begin{aligned} x^t&=s m(q^t), & y^t&=s n(r^t),\\ u^t&=ay^t, & v^t&=c^\top x^t. \end{aligned}\] define the instantaneous deviation gains and update the regret vectors by \[\begin{aligned} a i^t&=u i^t-(x^t)^\top u^t, & q i^{t+1}&=\max\{q i^t+a i^t,0\},\\ b j^t&=v j^t-(y^t)^\top v^t, & r j^{t+1}&=\max\{r j^t+b j^t,0\}. \end{aligned}\] the retained pair is updated using the strategies queried at j&\leq\bar{x}^\top c\bar{y}+\varepsilon, &&j=1,\ldots,n. \end{aligned}\] these requirements hold for every realization, rather than only in expectation or almost surely. \left\lceil \frac{20000 \cdot estimate with independent, identically distributed samples and centered sub-gaussian noise: its variance proxy is \(v {\mathrm{top}}\) along the first coordinate and \(v {\mathrm{rest}}\) in orthogonal directions, where \(0\leq v {\mathrm{rest}}\leq v {\mathrm{top}}\) . for \(\varepsilon>0\) , the goal is a measurable output \(\bar{x}\in e\) satisfying \(f(\bar{x})-f(x^\star)\leq\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(2/3\) over the algorithm and oracle randomness. the optimization problem is \[\min {x\in e} f(x).\] we use the euclidean inner product and norm, and index coordinates by \(0,\ldots,m\) . the algorithm receives \(m\) , the measurable sample space \(\omega\) , and \(g,r,v {\mathrm{top}},v {\mathrm{rest}},\varepsilon\) ; the objective and oracle distribution are accessible only through oracle replies. our assumptions: assumption 1 (convexity and lipschitz continuity). for every \(x,y\in e\) and \(s\in[0,1]\) , \[\begin{aligned} f((1-s)x+sy)&\leq(1-s)f(x)+sf(y),\\ |f(x)-f(y)|&\leq g\|x-y\|. \end{aligned}\] assumption 2 (bounded minimizer). there exists \(x^\star\in e\) such that \[\begin{aligned} f(x^\star)&\leq f(x) &&\text{for every }x\in e,\\ \|x^\star\|&\leq r. \end{aligned}\] assumption 3 (spiked sub-gaussian subgradient oracle). there are a probability measure \(p\) on \(\omega\) , a map template:
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.ProbabilityMeasure
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Prod

open MeasureTheory

namespace OracleTemplate

universe uP uD uI uQ uR uO

structure Algorithm (Query : Type uQ) (Reply : Type uR) (Output : Type uO) (numOracles : ℕ := 1) where
  Seed : Type := Unit
  [seedSpace : MeasurableSpace Seed]
  law : ProbabilityMeasure Seed := by exact ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac (), inferInstance⟩
  State : Type (max uQ uR uO)
  initial : Seed → State
  query : State → Fin numOracles × Query
  update : State → Reply → State
  output : State → Output

attribute [instance] Algorithm.seedSpace

structure Oracle (Query : Type uQ) (Reply : Type uR) (numOracles : ℕ := 1) where
  Seed : ℕ → Type := fun _ => Unit
  [seedSpace : ∀ k, MeasurableSpace (Seed k)]
  law : ProbabilityMeasure ((k : ℕ) → Seed k) := by
    exact ⟨MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac (fun _ => ()), inferInstance⟩
  answer : (history : List ((Fin numOracles × Query) × Reply)) →
    (Fin numOracles × Query) → Seed history.length → Reply

attribute [instance] Oracle.seedSpace

private def _run
    {Query : Type uQ} {Reply : Type uR} {Output : Type uO}
    {numOracles : ℕ}
    (oracle : List ((Fin numOracles × Query) × Reply) → (Fin numOracles × Query) → Reply)
    (A : Algorithm Query Reply Output numOracles) :
    Nat → List ((Fin numOracles × Query) × Reply) → (Fin numOracles → ℕ) → A.State →
      Output × List ((Fin numOracles × Query) × Reply)
  | 0, history, _, state => (A.output state, history)
  | k + 1, history, remaining, state =>
      let query := A.query state
      if remaining query.1 = 0 then (A.output state, history)
      else
        let reply := oracle history query
        let remaining := Function.update remaining query.1 (remaining query.1 - 1)
        _run oracle A k (history ++ [(query, reply)]) remaining (A.update state reply)

def executeWithTrace
    {Query : Type uQ} {Reply : Type uR} {Output : Type uO}
    {numOracles : ℕ}
    (oracle : Oracle Query Reply numOracles) (A : Algorithm Query Reply Output numOracles)
    (budget : Fin numOracles → ℕ) (seed : A.Seed := by exact ())
    (oracleSeed : (k : ℕ) → oracle.Seed k := by exact fun _ => ()) :
    Output × List ((Fin numOracles × Query) × Reply) :=
  _run (fun history query => oracle.answer history query (oracleSeed history.length))
    A (∑ i, budget i) [] budget (A.initial seed)

def execute
    {Query : Type uQ} {Reply : Type uR} {Output : Type uO}
    {numOracles : ℕ}
    (oracle : Oracle Query Reply numOracles) (A : Algorithm Query Reply Output numOracles)
    (budget : Fin numOracles → ℕ) (seed : A.Seed := by exact ())
    (oracleSeed : (k : ℕ) → oracle.Seed k := by exact fun _ => ()) : Output :=
  (executeWithTrace oracle A budget seed oracleSeed).1

structure Setup where
  numOracles : ℕ := 1
  Params : Type uP
  Public : Type uD
  Instance : Public → Type uI
  Query : Public → Type uQ
  Reply : Public → Type uR
  Output : Public → Type uO
  publicInput : Params → Public
  valid : Params → Prop
  admissible : (p : Params) → Instance (publicInput p) →
    Oracle (Query (publicInput p)) (Reply (publicInput p)) numOracles → Prop
  successful : {Ω : Type} → [MeasurableSpace Ω] →
    (p : Params) → Instance (publicInput p) →
    (Ω → Output (publicInput p)) → ProbabilityMeasure Ω → Prop :=
    fun _ _ _ _ => False
  allowedAlgorithm : (p : Public) → Algorithm (Query p) (Reply p) (Output p) numOracles → Prop :=
    fun _ _ => True

def Convergence (S : Setup)
    (budget : S.Params → Fin S.numOracles → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ makeAlgorithm : (p : S.Public) → Algorithm (S.Query p) (S.Reply p) (S.Output p) S.numOracles,
    (∀ p, S.valid p →
      ∀ (I : S.Instance (S.publicInput p))
        (oracle : Oracle (S.Query (S.publicInput p)) (S.Reply (S.publicInput p)) S.numOracles),
        S.admissible p I oracle →
          let A := makeAlgorithm (S.publicInput p)
          let result := fun seed : A.Seed × ((k : ℕ) → oracle.Seed k) =>
            execute oracle A (budget p) seed.1 seed.2
          S.successful p I result
            ⟨(A.law : Measure _).prod (oracle.law : Measure _), inferInstance⟩) ∧
    ∀ p, S.valid p → S.allowedAlgorithm (S.publicInput p) (makeAlgorithm (S.publicInput p))

end OracleTemplate
